title: What Is The Significance Of The Tabernacle In The Old Testament
paragraphs: The Significance of the Tabernacle in the Old Testament

The Tabernacle stands as one of the most profound symbols in the Old Testament, representing the dwelling place of God among His people. Understanding its significance helps illuminate the redemptive narrative of Scripture and points us forward to the person and work of Jesus Christ. Let’s explore how the Tabernacle reveals God’s character, His desire for relationship with humanity, and His plan for salvation.
1. God’s Desire to Dwell Among His People
The Tabernacle, also known as the “Tent of Meeting,” was commanded by God after the Israelites’ exodus from Egypt. Its very purpose was to provide a place where God could dwell among His people:
And let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them. -
Exodus 25:8 ASV

Unlike the distant, impersonal gods of the ancient world, the God of Israel desires a close relationship with His people. The Tabernacle was a physical sign of God’s presence and faithfulness, reassuring Israel that He was with them in their journey and struggles.
2. The Pattern of Worship and Sacrifice

The Tabernacle’s design and rituals established a pattern of worship centered on holiness, sacrifice, and atonement. The structure included the outer court, the Holy Place, and the Most Holy Place (Holy of Holies), each symbolizing different aspects of approaching God.

Access to the Most Holy Place, where the Ark of the Covenant resided, was restricted to the high priest and only once a year on the Day of Atonement. This emphasized both God’s holiness and humanity’s need for atonement:

And Jehovah said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place within the veil, before the mercy-seat which is upon the ark; that he die not: for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy-seat. -
Leviticus 16:2 ASV
The sacrificial system foreshadowed the ultimate sacrifice of Christ, who would provide full and final atonement for sin (see Hebrews 9:11-12 ASV).
3. The Tabernacle as a Foreshadowing of Christ
The New Testament reveals that every aspect of the Tabernacle pointed forward to Jesus. The Gospel of John declares:
And the Word became flesh, and dwelt among us (and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only begotten from the Father), full of grace and truth. -
John 1:14 ASV

The word “dwelt” (literally, “tabernacled”) shows that Jesus is the true Tabernacle—God’s ultimate presence among humanity. Through His sacrifice, the veil separating God and man is torn, granting believers direct access to God (Matthew 27:51 ASV; Hebrews 10:19-22 ASV).
4. A Model for God’s People Today

While the physical Tabernacle no longer stands, its principles remain. Believers are now called the temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 6:19 ASV), and the church is described as God’s dwelling place (Ephesians 2:22 ASV). The Tabernacle reminds us of God’s holiness, the need for cleansing from sin, and the privilege of His nearness through Christ.
Key Insights
The Tabernacle demonstrates God’s initiative to be present with His people.
The sacrificial system pointed to the necessity of atonement for sin.
Every element of the Tabernacle foreshadowed Christ, our ultimate High Priest and sacrifice.
Today, believers experience God’s indwelling presence through the Holy Spirit.
Conclusion

The Tabernacle is more than an ancient tent; it’s a rich symbol of God’s presence, holiness, and grace. It points us to Jesus Christ, who fulfills every aspect of the Tabernacle and offers us eternal access to God. Through faith in Him, we become living temples, testifying to the glory and love of God in the world.
